newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares little changed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares little changed in thin trade.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed almost unchanged on Sunday in what a bourse spokeswoman said was the lowest volume in recent years, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.01 percent, or 0.01 points, to 187.04 on extremely low turnover of 35 million shekels against 40 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.13 percent to 196.88.
"Activity is minimal despite the fact that share prices are very low. Investors are waiting for the U.S. presidential elections," said Michael Weiss at Evergreen Capital markets.
"A victory of President Bill Clinton will push the peace process and this may help the stock market," Weiss said.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the most active share, surged 4.0 percent to 138,999 on volume of 7.3 million shekels after its shares traded on Nasdaq gained 5.4 percent on Thursday and Friday.
The Israel Corp, the main loser on the Maof, fell 4.0 percent to 17,484 on very low volume of less than 60,000 shekels.
"The total turnover is simply ridiculous. I have never seen such a low volume and were it not for Teva the market would have closed lower," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

Other active shares include American Israeli Paper Mills Ltd, which gained 0.5 percent to 12,232 on turnover of 1.2 million shekels. Last Wednesday the company announced a cash dividend of $4.20 a share, reflecting capital gains due to a joint venture with Kimberly-Clark.
Clal Electronics Industries fell 1.25 percent to 24,807 on volume of one million shekels.
